bull.b: FDA alignment on a potential registrational path gives REO 033 a clearer development framework and could reduce regulatory uncertainty. If interim results are supportive, the planned Part B expansion may provide a more direct route toward accelerated and eventual full approval.

Fast Track designation provides regulatory recognition for pelareorep in a setting with no FDA-approved options after progression on first-line therapy. It may enable closer FDA interaction and support a more efficient development process if clinical evidence remains favorable.

Evidence that pelareorep can increase PD-L1, ICOSL, and CD8+ T-cell density supports its potential as a backbone therapy that improves immune access to tumors. This mechanism may broaden combination opportunities across difficult solid cancers.

bear.b: The absence of reported revenue means Oncolytics has not yet established a commercial cash-generating business, while widening losses show continued dependence on development financing. This limits internal funding capacity and leaves results highly dependent on clinical progress.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow indicates that ongoing research and development requires substantial funding before product commercialization. Increasing burn versus 2025 can shorten financial runway and raise the likelihood of further external capital needs.

Negative equity and a substantial decline in total assets indicate reduced financial flexibility as the company funds continued clinical development. Although absolute debt is low, the weakened balance sheet may constrain operations and increase reliance on new financing.
